options.text: Heating with concentrated nitric acid at room temperature
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:

Benzene is sulfonated with oleum to give benzenesulfonic acid ($C_6H_5SO_3H$). Acidification with dilute acid liberates phenol.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Positional Isomerism in Nitrophenol Acidity (Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers):
In the conjugate bases of 2-nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol, the negative charge delocalized around the ring resides directly on the carbons bearing the nitro group, allowing the nitro group to extend resonance delocalization onto its oxygen atoms ($-R$ effect). In 3-nitrophenol (meta), the negative charge never falls on the carbon bearing the nitro group; hence, only the weaker inductive ($-I$) effect operates.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

topic: Relative Acidity Order of Aliphatic Alcohols
questionText: What is the correct decreasing order of acidic strength among the following alcohols: water, methanol, ethanol, propan-2-ol, and 2-methylpropan-2-ol?

options.text: Water > Methanol > Ethanol ($1^\circ$) > Propan-2-ol ($2^\circ$) > 2-Methylpropan-2-ol ($3^\circ$)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Relative Acidity Order of Aliphatic Alcohols.

options.text: Ethanol > Propan-2-ol > 2-Methylpropan-2-ol > Water > Methanol
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Methanol > Water > 2-Methylpropan-2-ol > Propan-2-ol > Ethanol
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol ($3^\circ$) > Propan-2-ol ($2^\circ$) > Ethanol ($1^\circ$) > Methanol > Water
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers (Relative Acidity Order of Aliphatic Alcohols):
Water > Methanol > Ethanol ($1^\circ$) > Propan-2-ol ($2^\circ$) > 2-Methylpropan-2-ol ($3^\circ$)

Detailed Context:
The acidic character of alcohols is governed by the polarity of the $O-H$ bond and the stability of the conjugate alkoxide base ($RO^-$). Alkyl groups are electron-donating ($+I$ effect), which increases the electron density on oxygen and destabilizes the alkoxide anion. As alkyl substitution increases, acidity decreases: Water > $CH_3OH > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$ alcohol.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Basicity Comparison: Aniline vs Ammonia (Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers):
In aniline, the lone pair of electrons on nitrogen is conjugated with the $\pi$-electron system of the benzene ring. Resonance structures show that the lone pair is delocalized into the ortho and para positions of the ring ($C_6H_5-NH_2 \leftrightarrow$ quinonoid structures). Consequently, the electron density on nitrogen is significantly reduced compared to ammonia, making it less prone to accept a proton.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
